title: Water Inlet Fault
shortDescription: No water detected during fill phase.
fullDescription:
H01 on Toshiba dishwashers indicates water did not enter within the expected time. Check supply, hose kinks, and inlet valve.

Cycle is blocked.

fixSteps.title: Open supply
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure water supply valve is open.

fixSteps.title: Clean screen
fixSteps.instruction: Remove hose and clean screen filter.

title: Drain Fault
shortDescription: Dishwasher did not drain in time.
fullDescription:
H02 indicates drain timeout. Filter, hose, or pump are common causes.

Start with filter cleaning.

fixSteps.title: Check hose
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect drain hose and high loop.

fixSteps.title: Replace pump
fixSteps.instruction: Install new drain pump if needed.

faq.a: Yes, bail out before opening filter.

title: Heating Fault
shortDescription: Water did not heat to target temperature.
fullDescription:
H03 indicates the heater did not raise water temperature. Failed heater or thermistor.

Replace affected part.

title: Overfill / Leak Detected
shortDescription: Excess water detected in tub or base.
fullDescription:
H04 is the overfill/leak protection. Drain pump runs to evacuate water. Inspect for stuck inlet valve or leaks.

Shut off water supply first.

fixSteps.title: Inspect
fixSteps.instruction: Pull dishwasher to find leak source.

fixSteps.title: Fix or replace
fixSteps.instruction: Repair leak or replace inlet valve.

title: Turbidity Sensor Fault
fullDescription:
H05 indicates the turbidity sensor is unreliable. Cycle uses default length.

Cleaning may restore function.
whenToCallPro: If you cannot access the sump.

title: Thermistor Fault
shortDescription: Water temperature sensor open or shorted.
fullDescription: H06 indicates the water thermistor is failing. Replace sensor.
whenToCallPro: If sump access requires pulling unit.

faq.a: H06 is sensor fault; H03 is heating process fault.

title: Wash Motor Fault
fullDescription:
H07 indicates circulation motor did not reach speed or tripped overload. Clear debris and inspect motor.

Glass or foreign objects are common culprits.

faq.a: Often glass shards or bones in sump.

title: Door Switch Fault
shortDescription: Door switch or latch signal invalid.
fullDescription:
H08 indicates door switch inconsistency - door appears neither fully open nor fully closed.

Check alignment and replace switch if needed.

title: Communication Error
shortDescription: Main control and UI panel not communicating.
fullDescription:
H09 indicates loss of communication between boards. Reseat harnesses first.

May require board replacement.

fixSteps.title: Reseat harness
fixSteps.instruction: Open door and reseat ribbon cables.

fixSteps.title: Replace board
fixSteps.instruction: Install new UI or main PCB.

title: Main Control Fault
fullDescription:
H10 is a generic main board error. Power cycle; if persistent, replace the board.

May follow a power surge.
